title: ECG200 practical baseline and first Q.ANT-native PNN architecture
research_question: Can a first Q.ANT-native PNN-v1 architecture learn a real ECG time-series classification task, and how does it compare with a conventional neural baseline under the same fixed data split?

dataset.name: ECG200
dataset.split_policy: Use the canonical TRAIN/TEST split without resplitting.

hypothesis: A compact hierarchical PNN-v1 candidate built around Q.ANT KAN/Fourier-style nonlinear operations can learn useful structure in ECG200 while retaining a low-fan-in hierarchy motivated by the Toolkit discovery phase.

baseline.name: MLP-ReLU
baseline.purpose: Conventional neural baseline trained and evaluated on exactly the same ECG200 split.

pnn_candidate.name: PNN-v1-alpha1
principles: same input data and test set as baseline
pnn_candidate.note: Exact layer widths, preprocessing and training hyperparameters must be frozen in the Exp001 implementation before evaluation.

success_interpretation: Exp001 establishes whether the first PNN-v1 candidate can solve a real public time-series benchmark and provides a baseline for later architecture search. It is not designed to claim superiority from a single small dataset.
hardware_boundary: Q.ANT software/simulation-backend results are compatibility/model results, not measurements of real photonic latency, throughput, energy use, or hardware noise.
next_gate: Human review/approval before implementing and running PNN-v1 Exp001.
